problem_families.recognition_cues: Find foci, eccentricity, asymptotes of hyperbola
problem_families.first_technical_move: Extract a, b and compute e = sqrt(1 + b^2/a^2)
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Confusing transverse and conjugate axes

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Hyperbolic geometry and asymptotic analysis.

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Allowing eccentricity e <= 1 for a hyperbola.
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Hyperbola eccentricity must strictly satisfy e > 1.

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Introduction to 3D Geometry: Octants, Distance & Section Formulas

technical_core.canonical_statement: 3D space partitioned into 8 octants by xy, yz, zx planes; distance between P(x1,y1,z1) and Q(x2,y2,z2) is sqrt((x2-x1)^2+(y2-y1)^2+(z2-z1)^2).
technical_core.why_required: Generalization of Cartesian coordinates from 2D plane to 3D Euclidean space.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Z-coordinate omitted; 3D problems projected prematurely onto 2D planes.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Distance formula between two points in 3D

representations.name: Three-Dimensional Coordinate Frame Schematic
representations.math_encoded: Mutually perpendicular x, y, z axes with origin O(0,0,0) defining 8 octants and point P(x, y, z)
representations.common_incorrect_version: Left-handed coordinate frame without labelling
representations.verification_method: Verify right-hand rule x cross y = z

model_conditions.condition: Coordinate frame must follow right-handed system convention.
model_conditions.why_needed: Left-handed frames invert cross-product and orientation.
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Inconsistent vector and 3D angle formulas.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Plot point coordinates across x, y, z axes.
Apply 3D distance or section formula m:n.

required_transformations.description: Construct standard mathematical formulation for MATH-3D-INTRO

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Misidentifying octant signs of coordinates.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Generalizing 4 quadrants incorrectly to 8 octants.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Point (-2, 3, -4) placed in wrong octant.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Systematically trace signs of x, y, z to identify octant I through VIII.

mandatory_verifications: Verify consistency of MATH-3D-INTRO equations and boundary conditions.

problem_families.name: 3D Distance and Section Calculations
problem_families.recognition_cues: Find distance between 3D points or point of division
problem_families.first_technical_move: Apply 3D distance or section formula component-wise
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Omitting z-coordinate difference

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Three-dimensional Cartesian coordinate geometry.

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Omitting z-component in 3D distance formula.
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: 3D distance formula requires all three coordinates (x, y, z).

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Limits of Functions: Indeterminate Forms & Standard Limits

technical_core.canonical_statement: lim_{x->c} f(x) = L exists iff left-hand limit lim_{x->c^-} f(x) and right-hand limit lim_{x->c^+} f(x) both exist and are equal: LHL = RHL = L; standard limit lim_{x->0} sin(x)/x = 1.
technical_core.why_required: Rigorous definition of limit existence resolving 0/0 indeterminate forms.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Functions evaluated at singular points rather than investigating limiting behavior.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Fundamental trigonometric limit

representations.name: Left and Right Hand Limit Convergence Plot
representations.math_encoded: Curve y = f(x) with open circle at removable discontinuity (c, L) and arrows converging from left and right
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Open hole at singularity showing limit independent of f(c)
representations.common_incorrect_version: Showing f(c) must equal L for limit to exist

model_conditions.condition: x must be in radians for lim_{x->0} sin(x)/x = 1.
model_conditions.why_needed: In degrees, limit is pi/180.
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Calculus trigonometric derivative formulas fail by factor of 180/pi.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Evaluate functional form to check for 0/0 indeterminacy.
Factor algebraic terms or apply standard limit identities.
Verify LHL == RHL.

required_transformations.description: Construct standard mathematical formulation for MATH-CALC-LIMITS

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Conflating 0/0 indeterminate form with 0 or undefined.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Assuming 0 in numerator always equals 0.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: (x^2-4)/(x-2) at x=2 is 0/0, but limit is 4.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: 0/0 is indeterminate; factor or simplify before evaluating limit.

mandatory_verifications: Verify consistency of MATH-CALC-LIMITS equations and boundary conditions.

problem_families.name: Evaluating 0/0 Algebraic and Trig Limits
problem_families.recognition_cues: Find limit of rational or trig function at indeterminate point
problem_families.first_technical_move: Factorize numerator and denominator or apply lim sin x/x = 1
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Substituting x=0 directly and writing undefined

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Limit theory and indeterminate forms.

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Asserting limit exists when LHL != RHL.
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Limit exists if and only if left and right hand limits are equal.

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Derivatives: First Principles, Product, Quotient & Chain Rules

technical_core.canonical_statement: Derivative f'(x) = lim_{h->0} [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h represents instantaneous rate of change and slope of tangent to curve y = f(x).
technical_core.why_required: Foundation of differential calculus linking secant slopes to tangent slope.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Derivative treated as mechanical rule table without limiting slope foundation.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Definition of derivative from first principles

representations.name: Secant Line Limiting to Tangent Line Diagram
representations.math_encoded: Curve y = f(x) with secant line through (x, f(x)) and (x+h, f(x+h)) rotating into tangent line as h -> 0
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Rotation of secant into tangent as h approaches 0
representations.common_incorrect_version: Showing secant with fixed h
representations.verification_method: Verify slope of tangent equals derivative value

model_conditions.condition: Function must be continuous at x for derivative to exist.
model_conditions.why_needed: Discontinuity guarantees non-differentiability.
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Applying derivative rules across discontinuous jumps.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Form difference quotient [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h.
Expand and cancel h in denominator.
Take limit as h -> 0 to find f'(x).

required_transformations.description: Construct standard mathematical formulation for MATH-CALC-DERIVATIVES

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Believing (uv)' = u' v'.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Linear distribution fallacy across products.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Apply product rule: (uv)' = u'v + uv'.

mandatory_verifications: Verify consistency of MATH-CALC-DERIVATIVES equations and boundary conditions.

problem_families.name: Finding Derivative via First Principles
problem_families.recognition_cues: Compute derivative of polynomial, trig, or rational function from definition
problem_families.first_technical_move: Set up limit of difference quotient and cancel h
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Differentiating by rules when first principles requested

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Differential calculus and rate of change.

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Asserting (u*v)' = u' * v' in derivative calculations.
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Derivative of product requires product rule u'v + uv'.

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Measures of Dispersion: Variance & Standard Deviation

technical_core.canonical_statement: Variance sigma^2 = (1/N) sum (x_i - mu)^2 measures squared spread about mean; standard deviation sigma = sqrt(variance) restores original units.
technical_core.why_required: Second central moment measuring dispersion invariant under origin shifts.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Dispersion confused with central tendency.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Population variance formula

representations.name: Bell-Shaped Dispersion Spread Plot
representations.math_encoded: Data distribution showing mean mu at centre and intervals [mu-sigma, mu+sigma] capturing majority of spread
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Mean as central axis and sigma as spread metric
representations.common_incorrect_version: Showing negative variance
representations.verification_method: Verify sigma^2 >= 0 and units of sigma match data

model_conditions.condition: Variance is invariant under shift of origin (adding constant c), but multiplies by c^2 under scaling.
model_conditions.why_needed: Origin shift x_i + c shifts mean by c, leaving deviations x_i - mu unchanged.
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Incorrectly adding c to variance when data is shifted.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Compute arithmetic mean mu = (sum x_i)/N.
Compute sum of squared deviations sum (x_i - mu)^2.
Divide by N for variance and take square root for SD.

required_transformations.description: Construct standard mathematical formulation for MATH-STAT-VARIANCE-SD

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Adding c to variance when a constant c is added to each observation.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Confusing variance with mean under translation.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: If each score increases by 5, spread between students remains unchanged.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Variance is completely invariant under origin shift: Var(X + c) = Var(X).

mandatory_verifications: Verify consistency of MATH-STAT-VARIANCE-SD equations and boundary conditions.

problem_families.name: Variance and Standard Deviation Computation
problem_families.recognition_cues: Find variance and SD of discrete or grouped frequency data
problem_families.first_technical_move: Compute sum x_i and sum x_i^2 and apply sigma^2 = (sum x^2)/N - mu^2
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Subtracting mean before squaring and accumulating rounding errors

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Second central moment and data dispersion.

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Changing variance when a constant c is added to every observation.
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Variance is strictly invariant under addition of a constant.

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Axiomatic Probability, Conditional Probability & Bayes' Theorem

technical_core.canonical_statement: Conditional probability P(A|B) = P(A intersect B) / P(B) for P(B) > 0 restricts sample space to event B; Total Probability and Bayes theorem invert conditioning.
technical_core.why_required: Sample space contraction under given evidence.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Prior probability used when conditional evidence is present.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Conditional probability definition

symbols.name: Joint Probability
symbols.geometric_or_algebraic_role: Probability of both A and B

representations.name: Conditional Probability Venn Partition
representations.math_encoded: Sample space S containing events A and B with shaded intersection A cap B and restricted sample space B
representations.common_incorrect_version: Dividing by entire sample space S instead of P(B)

model_conditions.condition: Conditioning probability P(B) must be strictly positive (P(B) > 0).
model_conditions.why_needed: Conditional probability given impossible event is undefined.
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Division by zero error.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify joint event A intersect B and conditioning event B.
Compute P(A intersect B) and P(B).
Apply P(A|B) = P(A intersect B) / P(B).

required_transformations.description: Construct standard mathematical formulation for MATH-PROB-EVENTS

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Confusing P(A|B) with P(B|A).
misconceptions.why_plausible: Inverting conditioning order.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: P(Spade | Ace) = 1/4 != P(Ace | Spade) = 1/13.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: P(A|B) and P(B|A) are unequal unless P(A) = P(B).

mandatory_verifications: Verify consistency of MATH-PROB-EVENTS equations and boundary conditions.

problem_families.name: Conditional Probability and Bayes Inversion
problem_families.recognition_cues: Find probability of event given that another event has occurred
problem_families.first_technical_move: Calculate P(A cap B) and divide by P(B)
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Dividing by total sample space instead of P(B)

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Axiomatic conditional probability and Bayes analysis.

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Evaluating P(A|B) when P(B) = 0.
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Conditioning event must have strictly positive probability P(B) > 0.
